title: Sound Cues & Attenuation 🎛️
description: Build dynamic audio logic with Sound Cue nodes and control 3D distance falloff.

slides.title: Inside the Sound Cue Editor 🧪
slides.content:
# Audio Node Graph

Open any Sound Cue to see a canvas similar to the Material Editor. You connect **Sound Node** types:

* **Wave Player** – plays a single Sound Wave.
* **Random** – picks one of several sounds (great for footstep variations).
* **Mixer** – combines multiple sounds with volume control.
* **Modulator** – varies pitch/volume over time (engine RPM).
* **Delay** – adds silence before playback.
* **Attenuation** – distance falloff settings.

All paths eventually reach the **Output** node.

quizData.question: The Modulator node can change a sound's pitch dynamically.
quizData.explanation: Modulator varies pitch or volume based on a parameter, useful for engine sounds.

slides.title: Randomisation & Variation 🎲
slides.content:
## Avoid Repetition

To keep audio fresh, use:

* **Random Node** – hook up multiple Wave Players. Each time the cue plays, it randomly picks one.
* **Random Wave Player** (right‑click → Sound → Random Wave) – a single node that references multiple Sound Waves, picking one randomly.
* **Continuous Modulator** – vary pitch slightly each time to avoid the "machine gun" effect.

Example: a gunshot cue with 3 different bang sounds selected at random.

quizData.question: Which node picks one of several Wave Players at random each time?
quizData.explanation: The Random node outputs only one of its connected inputs, chosen at random.

slides.title: Attenuation: Distance Falloff 📉
slides.content:
# 3D Sound Control

An **Attenuation** node defines how a sound behaves in 3D space:

* **Attenuation (Distance)** – volume drops as you move away.
* **Spatialisation** – enables 3D positioning (panning).
* **Air Absorption** – high frequencies attenuate faster (realistic).
* **Occlusion** – muffles sound behind walls (requires Audio Volumes or raycasts).

Add an Attenuation node to your Sound Cue, then adjust the curve. Right‑click → **Create Attenuation Asset** to reuse settings.

*Analogy:* Attenuation is like a **volume knob tied to distance**.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Logarithmic Attenuation

For natural sound falloff, set the Attenuation Function to **Logarithmic** or **Natural Sound** in the Distance Settings.
